Verify: The driver is present and not banged out.

1. Attach and detach the keyboard rapidly. 
2. Open Device Manager -> Keyboards 
Note: Vary the number of times you rapidly detach/attach the keyboard for each iteration.

Verify: The keys and touchpad are working.

1. Open Device Manager and verify there are no banged out drivers.

1. Keyboard in an active position (Position B). 
2. Open Notepad or Wordpad.

Verify: All special keys are working (ie Volume, Brightness, etc.). These are located at the top of the keyboard and the FN lock must be turned off to access them. 
Verify: Windows key is working. Pressing it should open the Start menu. 
Verify: Right click key is working. 
Verify: Modifier keys are working. The modifiers are the Shift, Ctrl, and Alt. Open Notepad or Wordpad and type Shift+A for capital A, Ctrl+S to save the document and Alt+F to open the file menu.

testScenarios.objective: Keys and touchpad Use in All Positions
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
1. With keyboard attached move to all Positions (Positions A-E) 
2. In each position press some keys. 
3. In each position use the touchpad. 
Verify: The keys and touchpad work in Position B and upside down position B. 
Verify: The keys and touchpad do not work in all other positions.

testScenarios.objective: Keys and touchpad Use - Device Rotation
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
1. With keyboard attached and in an active position (Position B) 
2. Rotate device so it is in portrait mode - keyboard in an active position (Position E). 
Verify: The keys and touchpad are not working.

1. Attach keyboard in Position B. 
2. Move keyboard to Position C and then back to B. 
Verify: Keypresses working within 3 seconds.

1. Attach keyboard in an active position (Position B). 
2. Press the Caps Lock key several times. 
Verify: The Caps Lock LED turns on and off.

1. Attach keyboard in an active position (Position B). 
2. Open Notepad or Wordpad. 
3. Type characters with Caps Lock on and off. 
Verify: Capital and non-capital letters show correctly. 
4. With Caps Lock turned on detach and reattach the keyboard. 
5. Type some letters into Notepad or Wordpad. 
Verify: The letters typed are capital letters. 
6. With Caps Lock OFF, detach and reattach the keyboard. 
7. Type some letters into Notepad or Wordpad. 
Verify: The letters typed are lowercase letters.

testScenarios.objective: Caps Lock State maintained during CS
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
1. Attach keyboard in an Active position (Position B). 
2. Turn on Caps Lock. 
3. Press Power Button to go to CS. 
4. Wait 10 seconds and press Power Button to return to S0. 
5. Type a few characters into Notepad or Wordpad. 
Verify: The letters are capital letters. 
6. Repeat steps 1-5 with Caps Lock turned OFF. 
Verify: The letters typed are lower case.

testScenarios.objective: Caps Lock State maintained during Hibernate
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
1. Attach keyboard in an active position (Position B). 
2. Turn on Caps Lock. 
3. Hibernate the device. 
4. Wait 30 seconds and press Power Button to return to S0. 
5. Type a few characters into Notepad or Wordpad. 
Verify: The letters are capital letters. 
6. Repeat steps 1-5 with Caps Lock turned OFF. 
Verify: The letters typed are lower case.

testScenarios.objective: Fn Lock State maintained during CS.

testScenarios.objective: Fn Lock State maintained during Hibernate.

testScenarios.objective: KB - WLC Dock Pen, close lid, plug in PSU
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
1. Battery over 10%, PSU disconnected, blade connected with no pen, lid state B 
2. Pen battery over 75% but less than 100% 
3. Keep host in S0 -> dock pen 
4. Use SMonitorUAP command: SMonitorUAP.exe /wlcdevicestatus. 
Code shown as "0x02…....…." (Docked, Charging) 
Code shown as "0x01…........" (Docked, Not Charging) 
Verify: Pen is not charging 
5. Close to lid state A, host will enter CS 
6. Attach PSU, wait 10 minutes 
7. Open lid to state B, remove pen and click tail button to wake. 
Verify: Pen battery level has increased
